headline: South Korea KOSPI Falls Nearly 3% on Tech Sell-Off Despite Government Support
summary: South Korea's KOSPI index dropped 2.73% to 4,736.98, reaching its lowest level since January. A government pledge to deploy market stabilization funds failed to ease investor concerns over the tech sector.
why: South Korea's stock market is heavily weighted toward semiconductor giants, making it particularly vulnerable to global technology sell-offs.

impacts.name: KOSPI
impacts.why: Concerns over artificial intelligence valuations and global technology stocks dragged down South Korean equities.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Global technology sector weakness triggered heavy selling in South Korean semiconductor and tech shares.
